item.research_question: Can medium-entropy alloying be used to improve the thermoelectric performance of GeTe-based alloys?
item.material_system: GeTe-based alloys with compositions such as Ge0.63Mn0.15Pb0.1Sb0.06Cd0.06Te
item.processing_route: Medium-entropy alloying by co-alloying Mn, Pb, Sb, and Cd with GeTe
key_findings: A state-of-the-art zT of 2.1 at 873 K
High average zT ave value of 1.3 between 300 and 873 K
Lattice thermal conductivity of 0.30 W m−1 K−1 at 873 K
Seebeck coefficient of 197 µV K−1 at 300 K and 248 µV K−1 at 773 K
item.mechanism: The authors propose that medium-entropy alloying suppresses the phase transition, reduces lattice thermal conductivity, and enhances the Seebeck coefficient through band convergence and increased band effective mass
item.limitations: The authors note that high-entropy alloying can lead to degraded carrier mobility, which needs to be compensated by band engineering
item.future_work: The authors suggest that further optimization of the alloy composition and microstructure could lead to even higher thermoelectric performance
quotes: The power of medium-entropy thermoelectrics is exploited in GeTe by co-alloying Mn, Pb, Sb, and Cd to optimize the delicate trade-offs between the carrier mobility, crystal structure, and lattice thermal conductivity

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can medium-entropy alloying be used to improve the thermoelectric performance of GeTe-based alloys?. System: GeTe-based alloys with compositions such as Ge0.63Mn0.15Pb0.1Sb0.06Cd0.06Te. Processing: Medium-entropy alloying by co-alloying Mn, Pb, Sb, and Cd with GeTe. Test conditions: Temperature range of 300-873 K. Findings: A state-of-the-art zT of 2.1 at 873 K; High average zT ave value of 1.3 between 300 and 873 K; Record high Vickers hardness of 270; Lattice thermal conductivity of 0.30 W m−1 K−1 at 873 K; Seebeck coefficient of 197 µV K−1 at 300 K and 248 µV K−1 at 773 K. Mechanism: The authors propose that medium-entropy alloying suppresses the phase transition, reduces lattice thermal conductivity, and enhances the Seebeck coefficient through band convergence and increased band effective mass. Limitations: The authors note that high-entropy alloying can lead to degraded carrier mobility, which needs to be compensated by band engineering. Future work: The authors suggest that further optimization of the alloy composition and microstructure could lead to even higher thermoelectric performance. Quote: "The power of medium-entropy thermoelectrics is exploited in GeTe by co-alloying Mn, Pb, Sb, and Cd to optimize the delicate trade-offs between the carrier mobility, crystal structure, and lattice thermal conductivity"
